lines.trans: Welcome back. How did your fundraising go today?
Hey, stop! What is wrong with you all of a sudden? Don't treat me like a fool!
Even you too...
Anyone would hate being treated so crudely in a place like this!
I am not an object.
If you're going to hold me, then hold me properly.
I made up my mind to stay with you, Mr. Muranishi. I can trust you, right?
Every single person is so selfish. It wears my spirit down.

words.gram: Noun in the idiom 気が向く (feel like doing).

lines.trans: Nobody understands how hard I'm working myself to the bone for this company.
Are you doing all this just so someone will understand you?
Just because you're exhausted, don't put yourself down like that.
Thank you.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

examples.text: お疲れさまです。どうでした？成果のほうは。
examples.trans: Welcome back. How did your fundraising go today?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: こんなとこで雑にされるの、誰だってイヤです！
examples.trans: Anyone would hate being treated so crudely in a place like this!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 抱くなら真面目に抱いてください。
examples.trans: If you're going to hold me, then hold me properly.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Mental readiness to face something difficult or risky.

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Ichidan verb; potential form 決められる means 'can decide'.

examples.text: まだ何も決めていません。
今決められないなら、後で考えましょう。
examples.trans: If you can't decide now, let's think about it later.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; potential form 信じられる means 'can believe' (信じられない = unbelievable).

examples.text: あなたの言葉を信じます。
そんなこと、信じられません。
examples.trans: I can't believe such a thing.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: どいつもこいつも自分勝手だ。気が滅入るよ。
examples.trans: Every single person is so selfish. It wears my spirit down.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

examples.text: 俺がどれだけ会社のために粉骨砕身やってるか、誰も分かってない。
examples.trans: Nobody understands how hard I'm working myself to the bone for this company.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: 疲れてるからって、自分を卑下しすぎないで。
examples.trans: Just because you're exhausted, don't put yourself down like that.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Compound ichidan verb formed from する + すぎる.

examples.text: 最近働きすぎています。
examples.trans: I've been working too much lately.

examples.text: 心配しすぎないでください。

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
